findings.description: aggregate_status drops the directory-name exclusion (`! -path "$SUITE_DIR/screen-*"`) and relies solely on `map(select(.screen != true))`. The diff does not show write_status emitting a `screen` key, and test RA-11 fabricates the marker with jq instead of running a real `--screen` batch, so the test cannot detect a missing marker.
findings.failure_mode: If per-batch STATUS.json for `--screen` runs lacks `screen: true` (or writes it as the string "true"), every screen batch now leaks into the suite-level STATUS.json: trials_planned inflates, screen cuts appear in `cuts`, and `state` can flip to failed/partial from a screen run. Previously the path filter excluded them regardless.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm write_status writes `screen: $SCREEN` as a JSON boolean (via --argjson, not --arg). Add a test that runs `--screen` for real and then a normal batch, asserting the screen batch is absent from the aggregate.

findings.description: `sys.exit(1 if skipped else 0)` makes exit 1 mean both "a named file is unreadable" and "total is a lower bound". A single malformed ledger line now yields a non-zero exit even though a complete JSON object was printed to stdout.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller doing `json=$(spend.sh --json) || die` (a budget gate in run-arms.sh or CI) now aborts on one bad ledger line and discards the JSON that already carries `complete: false`. Callers cannot distinguish unreadable input from a partial total.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a distinct exit code for INCOMPLETE (e.g. 3) and document it, or keep exit 0 under --json since `complete` already carries the signal. Audit callers of spend.sh for `|| die` patterns before merging.

findings.description: `($ph.models_used // {} | objects // {}) | keys[]` turns a non-object models_used into `{}`, and the row output also emits `models_used: {}`. The header spec says degraded is true when "a models_used key differs from model_requested"; an array shape like `["claude-opus-5-5"]` silently disables that check and discards the model ids from the row.
findings.failure_mode: A phase that ran on a different model than requested is recorded as not degraded and with empty models_used whenever the producer emits a list instead of a map. The new test codifies this as expected behavior, so the signal loss is invisible.
findings.suggested_fix: Handle arrays explicitly: `($ph.models_used | if type == "object" then keys elif type == "array" then map(tostring) else [] end)`, and emit the array converted to `{id: null}` or preserve it under a separate key rather than replacing with `{}`.

findings.description: The brbuild stage is removed but the diff does not show the rest of the Dockerfile. The new test asserts one FROM and no `AS brbuild`, but does not assert the absence of a `COPY --from=brbuild` consumer.
findings.failure_mode: If any `COPY --from=brbuild` line remains, `docker build` fails with an invalid from flag. The bats test would still pass since it only greps for the stage definition.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `! grep -q -- '--from=brbuild' "$df"` to the Dockerfile test, and confirm the image builds once before merging.

findings.description: The leftover-workdir assertion scans the shared `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}` for any `ablation-row.*` newer than the fixture. Under `bats --jobs N`, or when another ablation-row.sh runs concurrently on the host, an unrelated live work directory matches.
findings.failure_mode: Intermittent CI failure of an otherwise passing test, unrelated to the code under test.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the row build with `TMPDIR="$T/tmp"` (create it in setup) and assert that directory is empty afterwards, so the check is scoped to this test's process.
